segments.title: Five jobs in one Mardi Gras day
segments.summary: Laine describes playing five engagements in a single Mardi Gras day, from advertising for a doctor to parades and a ball, while a visitor departs.

segments.title: Playing advertising wagons and Wild West show corners
segments.summary: Laine recalls advertising wagons for fights, balls and football, a clarinetist's torn pants story, and playing on corners near a Wild West show.

segments.title: Black bands in the city: Green, Perez and a military band
segments.summary: Asked about colored bands, Laine remembers Green's band and a short yellow leader's military band that played funerals, and Perez as a bandleader.

segments.title: Tom Ehrle and the Rosenmeiers
segments.summary: Allen asks about Tom Ehrle, a guitar and bass player who worked for Laine; Rosenmeier is not known to Laine.

segments.title: The Korns and the Biloxi Elks Convention
segments.summary: Laine recalls Marcus and Marty Korn, trombone and clarinet, who worked with him, including a three-day Elks Convention job in Biloxi; he cannot remember all his musicians.

segments.title: Managing many bands and training young players
segments.summary: Laine explains that Manuel Marlowe, Vega and his son ran bands under his instructions, then recalls the first kids he taught horn and how the Brunies boys lived at his home.

segments.title: B-flat cornets and low pitch for dance halls
segments.summary: Laine says all cornets were B-flat except Johnny Provanzano's Italian E-flat, and that bands used low pitch indoors and high pitch on the street.

segments.title: Photographs: Cordello, Babe Regis and Ebronis
segments.summary: Looking at a band photograph, they identify Charlie Cordello, Babe Regis and others; Cordello no longer plays.

segments.title: Happy Schilling and marching band photos
segments.summary: They identify George Schilling in a photo, a marching band on a city street, and a recent yard photo with Laine on drum.

segments.title: The Brunies family and a note from Gussie Mueller
segments.summary: Photos of the many Brunies brothers, a doubtful Harry Shields identification, and a note from Gussie Mueller saying he got his first break with Laine.

segments.title: Playing Lake Pontchartrain, Washington Garden and Bucktown
segments.summary: Laine played Sundays and Wednesdays at Washington Garden, an old hotel at the lake, and describes Bucktown's dancing pavilions and the crowds.

segments.title: Brownlee, Lala and Emmett Hardy across the river
segments.summary: Laine cannot recall many musicians by name; he knew of Emmett Hardy but never played with him, having led a band there long before.

segments.title: Closing remarks and the club meeting
segments.summary: Allen thanks Laine, who says he enjoys the visit and the sociable club he belongs to.

segments.title: Unrelated blues record
segments.summary: Recorded blues song lyrics unrelated to the interview.
